findings.title: import() calls in the object literal run eagerly, so every app still loads at module evaluation
findings.body: Each entry is `import("./x")` evaluated directly in the object literal. All ~29 dynamic imports start the moment `@calcom/app-store` is first imported, so every app package is still loaded on first use of the store. This gives no lazy loading, and the module graph still pulls in every app. It also adds overhead: the promises are created up front, and call sites must now `await` them. An app whose import fails produces an unhandled rejection at startup. It then rejects on every later lookup instead of being skipped. To get lazy behaviour, store thunks (`() => import("./x")`) and invoke only the one needed.

findings.title: async forEach callback inside try/catch: errors are no longer caught and deletions are not awaited
findings.body: The callback was made `async` so it can `await getCalendar(...)`. `forEach` ignores the returned promise, so the surrounding `try/catch` can no longer catch a `getCalendar` failure or a `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` rejection. Previously a synchronous throw from `getCalendar` was caught and logged. Now the error becomes an unhandled promise rejection. The function also continues to send emails and returns `true` before the calendar and video deletions finish. In serverless environments the work can be cut off. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` inside the try block.

findings.title: async forEach callback inside try/catch: errors are no longer caught and deletions are not awaited
findings.body: Same issue as the vital reschedule. `forEach(async ...)` discards the promises, so the `try/catch` around it is now dead for any rejection from `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`; these become unhandled rejections. The reschedule flow does not wait for the external deletions before sending emails and returning. Replace with `await Promise.all(refs.map(async ...))` so errors are logged and the work completes.

findings.title: requestReschedule: async forEach leaves calendar/video deletions unawaited and rejections unhandled
findings.body: Making the `forEach` callback async to `await getCalendar` means the mutation neither awaits nor handles failures of `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent` or `deleteMeeting`. There is no `try/catch` here at all. A failing integration produces an unhandled rejection, which can crash the Node process or be silently dropped. The mutation also returns, after sending emails and webhooks, before the external events are actually removed. Collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)`, with error handling.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel path pushes into apiDeletes from an unawaited async forEach, after Promise.all has already run
findings.body: In the `allRemainingBookings` branch, `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` is not awaited. It also pushes the resolved result rather than the promise. `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs later and sees an `apiDeletes` array that these callbacks have not populated yet. The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are therefore never awaited, and their failures are unhandled rejections. Adding `await getCalendar` inside the callback delays the first `deleteEvent` call further, so a response (or serverless freeze) can happen before any deletion starts. Replace with a `for...of` loop or `Promise.all(map(...))` and push the promises.
